Deprecation.description: Only when this deployment deprecates the operation (ADR-022): `@` and the time of the deprecation in seconds since 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z (RFC 9745). A `Link` header with `rel="deprecation"` may point at the migration notes.

Sunset.description: Only when a deprecated operation has a removal date: the time after which it may stop working, as an HTTP date (RFC 8594). At least 180 days after the Deprecation date (ADR-022).

X-Listing-Guard-Version.description: The release version of the server that answered, for example `0.8.0`; `dev` for a build without a release version. On every response under /api/v1 (ADR-022). Use it to fetch the contract of that release; it is not for feature detection (see GET /api/v1/capabilities).

fixes.description: Whether `POST /api/v1/checks` returns verified fix suggestions and readiness.

packs.description: The analysis packs this deployment serves over HTTP, sorted by id. `batch`, `policy-analyzer` and `sheet-connector` are not listed: they have no endpoint here.

plans.description: Whether plans and the monthly quota are applied in this deployment.

trademarkCatalog.description: The trademark catalog this deployment serves. Only its state, never its name.

state.description: `READY`, `DISABLED` (no catalog is configured) or `REFUSED` (the configured one cannot be served).

version.description: The catalog version, only while the state is `READY`.

end.description: End of the span (UTF-16 code units, exclusive).

field.description: Which value the finding is about.

kind.description: The case inside the rule; stable like ruleId.

label.description: The label the client gave the value, or null.

message.description: Human text, currently Vietnamese, with the real characters, positions and numbers.

severity.description: WARNING (worth a look before production) or INFO. No ERROR: nothing here is backed by an official source.

sourceStatus.description: How well the rule is backed by documentation. Always UNVERIFIED today: it is an internal print policy.

start.description: Start of the span in the text as sent (UTF-16 code units, inclusive).

suggestion.description: Human text, currently Vietnamese. Never proposes a replacement value.

value.description: The offending characters, at most a few; null for a finding that keeps no text (too long, spaces).

listing.description: The listing in the marketplace's own JSON format (for Etsy, Open API v3 style snake_case fields; for Amazon, title, brand, bullet_points, description, search_terms, product_type, price, quantity, images). Must be a JSON object.

marketplace.description: Marketplace code, case-insensitive. Supported: ETSY, AMAZON.

analysisVersion.description: Version of the whole analysis that produced the result. Currently equal to rulesetVersion; it will also change when other analyzers (for example an LLM step) are added. Two checks with the same marketplace, contentHash and analysisVersion have the same result.

cached.description: True when an identical listing had already been checked with the same analysisVersion and the stored result is returned instead of a new check.

checkId.description: Identifier of the stored check; use it with GET /api/v1/checks/{id}.

contentHash.description: SHA-256 of the normalized listing content.

createdAt.description: When the check was first stored.

fixesComputed.description: Whether verified fixes were computed for this result.

readiness.description: Readiness from the listing-rules pack only; null when this legacy result has not been enriched.

rulesetVersion.description: Version of the ruleset that produced the findings. Null for checks stored before versions were recorded.

complete.description: True when every pack that deletes results can still show every day of the period.

retention.description: The packs that delete their results; `listing-rules` is not among them: its results are not deleted.

text.description: A sentence that says it in words.

distinctRules.description: Every rule with a false positive in the period, before the list is cut.

items.description: Most false positives first, then most verdicts, then pack and rule id by code point.

limit.description: The most items the list holds (`listing-guard.reports.top-rules`).

verdicts.description: Every verdict on this rule in the period.

checkId.description: The `checkId` of the stored result, as POST or GET of that pack returned it.

findingIndex.description: The index of the finding in that result's `findings`, from 0, in the order GET returns them.

note.description: An optional note of at most 280 characters. Do not paste listing text into it. Blank is no note.
note.example: The word is part of the product name.

pack.description: The pack of the result: `listing-rules`, `trademark-risk` or `variation-checks`.

analysisVersion.description: The analysisVersion of the result the finding belongs to.

created.description: True when this call stored the first verdict of this API key on the finding; false when it replaced an earlier one.

level.description: The finding's severity (`ERROR`, `WARNING`, `INFO`) or trademark risk (`HIGH`, `MEDIUM`, `LOW`).

note.example: The word is part of the product name.

source.description: `RULE`, `CATALOG` (a trademark finding that matched a catalog mark) or `WATCHLIST` (reserved).

byReviewer.description: One entry per reviewer who gave a verdict in the period, most verdicts first.

byRule.description: One entry per rule and source that had a finding or a verdict in the period: most false positives first, then most verdicts, then most findings, then pack and rule id.

marketplace.description: The marketplace the counts are limited to, or null for all.

period.description: The days counted, in UTC, both ends included.

totals.description: Every verdict given in the period.

byVerdict.description: Verdicts per verdict; `CORRECT`, `FALSE_POSITIVE` and `NOT_USEFUL` are always present.

falsePositiveRate.description: `FALSE_POSITIVE / verdicts`, four decimals; null when there is no verdict.

field.description: Field path, see the integration guide.

fix.description: A verified suggestion for this finding; null when no certain fix exists.

message.example: Tag 'a tag that is far too long...' dài 38 ký tự, tối đa 20.

suggestion.example: Rút ngắn tag này ít nhất 18 ký tự.

value.description: The value that caused the finding; null when no single value applies (a missing field).
value.example: a tag that is far too long for the limit

enabled.description: True when `POST /api/v1/checks` adds verified fix suggestions and `listing-rules` readiness.

byWeek.description: The same numbers per ISO week, in order, without gaps (a week with no result is all zeros). The first and the last week are clipped to the period and marked `partial` when the ISO week is longer.

coverageNote.description: Which packs delete their results, after how long, and so from which day their numbers are complete.

feedback.description: Verdicts that reviewers gave on findings in the period (ADR-034), for the whole period only.

generatedAt.description: When the report was computed. A result of a pack that deletes results is counted only if it was still stored at this instant.

marketplace.description: The marketplace the counts are limited to (`ETSY` or `AMAZON`), or null for all.

packs.description: The numbers of each pack over the whole period.

period.description: The days counted, in UTC, both ends included.

reaudit.description: The periodic re-audits of the console in the period (ADR-035), for the whole period only. Counts only: no listing, SKU or finding text is in it.

versions.description: What runs now. Results of the period may have been made under older versions.

analysisVersion.description: Version of everything that decides the result (ruleset, algorithm versions, the image runtime). Opaque: compare for equality only. Two checks of one client with the same marketplace, profile, images and metadata and the same analysisVersion have the same result.

cached.description: True when the stored result of an identical earlier check is returned instead of a new analysis. Only a COMPLETE result is ever returned from the cache.

checkId.description: Identifier of the stored check; use it with GET /api/v1/image-checks/{id} until expiresAt.

completeness.description: COMPLETE when every check ran on every image. INCOMPLETE when one did not (failedRules names it; an image that cannot be decoded, or a threshold the ruleset does not have yet, is such a case): the findings that were established are kept. An INCOMPLETE result is never a clean result, is never reused and costs no quota.

createdAt.description: When the check was first stored (UTC).

disclaimer.description: Statement that the result is a reference warning and not a statement of the marketplace. Show it with the result.

expiresAt.description: When the stored result stops being readable (UTC). After this instant GET answers 404 and the same images are analysed again.

failedRules.description: Checks that did not run: a pack-level rule id such as image_count, or images[i].rule for one image. Empty when none failed.

findings.description: Findings about the set of images as a whole, such as the image count.

images.description: One entry per submitted image, in the order of the request.

profile.description: The image profile that was used; the default when the request named none.

rulesetVersion.description: Version of the image ruleset that produced the result.

summary.description: The outcome the ruleset maps from the highest severity found (for example READY, REVIEW, BLOCK); always INCOMPLETE when completeness is INCOMPLETE. A summary, not a verdict of the marketplace.

completeness.description: INCOMPLETE when a check could not run on this image, for example it could not be decoded.

failedRules.description: Checks that did not run on this image.

imageHash.description: SHA-256 of the submitted bytes, lower-case hex.

metadata.description: Absent when the image could not be decoded.

ordinal.description: Zero-based position of the image in the request.

source.description: Where the client declared the image came from; UNKNOWN when it declared none.

enabled.description: False when the rule is switched off for this product type: nothing is enforced and the number is only on record. A counter should not enforce a limit that is not enabled.

field.description: The field of the standard input (`docs/input-schema.md`) the limit applies to, such as `title`, `tags`, `bullet_points` or `search_terms`. For a list field, `MAX_COUNT` limits the list and `MAX_LENGTH` or `MAX_BYTES` limit each item. A field inside the Etsy `personalization` block is a path: `[]` stands for every question, and `[type=DROPDOWN]` or `[type=UPLOAD]` for the questions of that type, for example `personalization.questions[].question_text`.

kind.description: What is limited: `MAX_LENGTH` (length of a text, or of each item of a list), `MAX_COUNT` (number of items of a list, or of words of a text), `MAX_BYTES` (size in UTF-8 bytes) or `MAX_OCCURRENCES` (how often the same word or character may appear).

ruleId.description: The rule that enforces the limit; the `ruleId` of its findings.

severity.description: How a finding that breaks the limit is rated.

sourceStatus.description: How well the number is backed by the marketplace's documentation: `VERIFIED`, `SECONDARY` or `UNVERIFIED`.

unit.description: What is counted, as the rule counts it: `CODE_POINTS` (an emoji counts once, not the UTF-16 length of a JavaScript string), `ITEMS`, `WORDS`, `UTF8_BYTES` or `OCCURRENCES`.

checks.description: Stored results created in the period.

findings.description: Findings per severity; the three severities are always present.

pack.description: The pack id; present on the period totals only.

readiness.description: The publish readiness stored with the results (ADR-014).

statuses.description: Results per stored status; every status is present.

topRules.description: The rules with the most findings; present on the period totals only.

MarkCountView.description: A mark of the trademark catalog (the catalog's own display text, never text from a listing).

checksAffected.description: Results with at least one finding for this mark.

highestRisk.description: The highest risk among the findings for this mark.

distinctMarks.description: Every different mark in the period, before the list is cut.

items.description: Most findings first, then most results affected, then the mark by code point.

format.description: JPEG or PNG, read from the bytes, never from the file name or the content type.

hadAlpha.description: The image has an alpha channel; it was composited onto white for the checks.

hadIccProfile.description: The image has an embedded ICC profile; it was converted to sRGB for the checks.

height.description: Height in pixels after the orientation was applied.

orientation.description: EXIF orientation of the file, 1 when it has none.

width.description: Width in pixels after the orientation was applied.

available.description: Whether the pack can answer now. False for `trademark-risk` while the catalog is not READY; the endpoint then answers `503 trademark-not-configured`.

rulesetVersions.description: The version of the active ruleset per marketplace (upper case, sorted): the `rulesetVersion` of a result.

marketplace.description: Marketplace code, case-insensitive. Supported: ETSY, AMAZON.

print_profile.description: The code of a print profile declared in the ruleset. Absent means the ruleset's default profile. An undeclared code is a 400 (`unknown-print-profile`), never replaced by the default.

product_type.description: Free text naming the product, for example "jersey". Hashed and not read by any rule yet.

values.description: What the buyer typed, one entry per field of the order: objects with `label` (optional, the name of the field, for example "name") and `text`. The text is NOT trimmed: spaces are reported, not removed. Entries that are not objects or have no text are dropped.

analysisVersion.description: Version of everything that decides the result (ruleset, code versions, trademark ruleset and catalog). Opaque: compare for equality only. Two screenings of one client with the same marketplace, the same values and the same analysisVersion have the same result.

cached.description: True when the stored result of an identical earlier screening is returned instead of a new analysis. Only a COMPLETE result is ever returned from the cache.

checkId.description: Identifier of the stored screening; use it with GET /api/v1/personalization-screenings/{id} until expiresAt.

completeness.description: COMPLETE when every character rule ran and the trademark scan finished. INCOMPLETE when a character rule failed (failedRuleIds names it), the trademark scan failed, or no trademark catalog is served (trademark.status NOT_CONFIGURED): the findings that were established are kept. An INCOMPLETE result is never a clean result, is never reused and costs no quota.

disclaimer.description: Statement that the result is a reference warning and not a statement of the print workshop, a marketplace or a court. Show it with the result.

failedRuleIds.description: Character rules that failed; empty when none did.

findings.description: The findings of the character rules, value by value.

printProfile.description: The print profile that was used; the ruleset's default when the request named none.

rulesetVersion.description: Version of the personalization ruleset that produced the result.

summary.description: Number of character findings per severity (the trademark findings are counted by their risk level).

trademark.description: The trademark scan of the same values. Show it next to the character findings: neither replaces the other.

completeness.description: Results per completeness; both values are present.

findings.description: Character-rule findings per severity; the three severities are always present.

pack.description: The pack id; present on the period totals only.

topRules.description: The character rules with the most findings; present on the period totals only.

trademarkRiskLevels.description: Results per risk level of their trademark scan; `UNKNOWN` is never counted as `LOW`.

trademarkStatus.description: Results per state of their trademark scan: `COMPLETE`, `INCOMPLETE` or `NOT_CONFIGURED` (no catalog was served).

enforced.description: True when plans are on: packs are limited by plan and new results count against a monthly quota (read `GET /api/v1/usage` for the calling client). False: nothing is limited.

averageScore.description: The mean score of the scored results, one decimal; null when there are none.

checksWithReadiness.description: Results with a readiness: scored plus incomplete.

incompleteChecks.description: Results whose readiness is `INCOMPLETE` (a rule failed): stored as not ready, with no score.

readyRate.description: `readyChecks / checksWithReadiness`, four decimals; null when there is no readiness.

versions.description: The readiness versions found in the period; present on the period totals only. A mean over two versions is not a trend.

clients.description: Clients that ran at least one.

listingsChecked.description: Listings read and checked, all runs together (a listing counts once per run).

runs.description: Runs that started in the period.

scopesToReaudit.description: Scopes (client, marketplace, account label) whose latest run was made with another catalog than the one served now, so a new run is due. Null when no catalog is served. Counted over all time, not the period.

servedCatalog.description: The catalog version this deployment serves now; null when none is served.

coveredFrom.description: The first day for which every result of the pack is still stored.

period.description: How long a result is kept, as an ISO-8601 duration, from the configuration.

id.description: The account id, or the public key id of the API key. Never an e-mail.

from.description: The level the rule assigned before any adjustment.

reason.description: `outside_product_classes`: the request named a product type and none of the mark's Nice classes is one of the product type's. `common_word`: the mark is an ordinary word of the ruleset's list and the match is not an exact or phrase match in a brand field. `llm_descriptive`: a language model read the sentence around the match and thinks the word describes the product (only when the operator turned the LLM judge on, ADR-036); the finding is kept and its note starts with the label.

to.description: The level this reason alone gives; lower than `from`.

checksAffected.description: Results with at least one such finding.

severity.description: A rule stored at two severities appears twice.

falsePositiveRate.description: `falsePositive / verdicts`, four decimals; null when there is no verdict.

findings.description: Findings of this rule in the results created in the period (retained packs: only while kept).

source.description: `RULE`, `CATALOG` (a trademark finding that matched a catalog mark) or `WATCHLIST` (reserved).

distinctRules.description: Every different rule and severity in the period, before the list is cut.

items.description: Most findings first, then most results affected, then the rule id by code point, then the severity.

limit.description: The most items the list holds.

limits.description: Every numeric limit of the ruleset's rules, in rule order. A rule that is switched off is listed with `enabled` false. Read the limits you need by `field` and `kind`, and ignore the ones you do not know.

marketplace.description: The marketplace code, in upper case.

productType.description: The product type asked for, trimmed and as sent; null when none was asked for.

rulesetVersion.description: The version of the ruleset the limits come from; the same value as `rulesetVersion` of a check. Opaque: compare for equality, do not parse.

checksAffected.description: Results with at least one finding of this severity.

sourceId.description: The source id the link was built from.

url.description: The address. Built from a template of the ruleset, only for a source the ruleset names.

demo.description: True when the configured catalog is the DEMO catalog of invented marks: a trademark result is then not real.

state.description: `READY`: trademark checks are served. `DISABLED`: no catalog is configured. `REFUSED`: a catalog is configured but cannot be served. In the last two the risk of a listing is unknown, never low.

end.description: End of the span in the field text (UTF-16 code units, exclusive).

field.description: Field path: title, description, brand, search_terms, tags[i], bullet_points[i] (zero-based, in the cleaned list: blank entries are dropped).

insideColorPhrase.description: The match lies inside a color description. This explains the finding and never lowers its level.

mark.description: The catalog mark that matched; null for a finding that has no mark.

matchType.description: How it was found: EXACT, PHRASE, FUZZY (similar to a mark) or CONTEXT (a rule about place, sport or color).

otherRuleIds.description: Other rules that matched an overlapping span of the same field and lost to this finding.

risk.description: Level of this finding: LOW (informational), MEDIUM or HIGH.

score.description: Similarity from 0 to 1: 1.0 for EXACT and PHRASE, the final score for FUZZY, null for CONTEXT.

snippet.description: The text of the span, cut to a length limit.

source.description: Where the finding comes from: CATALOG (a mark of the catalog), CONTEXT (a rule about place, sport or color) or WATCHLIST (an entry of the client's own watchlist, rule `watchlist_match`, ADR-031).

sourceIds.description: Ids of the source records of the catalog mark; empty when there is no mark.

sourceLinks.description: Public look-up pages for the source records, one per source id the ruleset has an address for (today an id `uspto:<serial number>` links to its USPTO TSDR page); empty when none has. A link is built from the ruleset and is not checked: open it to read the record, and treat it as unverified.

start.description: Start of the span in the field text (UTF-16 code units, inclusive).

tsdrStatuses.description: The last status the USPTO TSDR gave for the source records of the mark, one entry for each source id that has been checked. **Present only when the deployment turned it on (`listing-guard.trademark.tsdr.finding-status.enabled`); absent otherwise.** When present it can be empty. It is information read when this answer is built, not part of the stored result: it never changes `risk`, `analysisVersion` or the cache, and the same stored result can show a newer status later. Read `checkedAt`: the status can be old.

watchlistEntry.description: The watchlist entry the finding comes from; null for any finding whose `source` is not WATCHLIST.

listing.description: The listing in the marketplace's own JSON format, exactly as for POST /api/v1/checks. Must be a JSON object.

marketplace.description: Marketplace code, case-insensitive. Supported: ETSY, AMAZON.

product_type.description: Optional. What kind of product the listing sells: one of the product types the active trademark ruleset declares (see the integration guide), written exactly as declared. When it is given, a catalog match whose mark has Nice classes, none of them one of the product type's classes, is reported one level lower and the finding says so in `riskAdjustments`; a mark with no Nice class is never lowered. A value the ruleset does not declare is refused with 400 `unknown-product-type`, never ignored. Leave it out to get the result without product classes. It is not the Amazon `product_type` of the listing, and it is part of what makes two requests identical for the cache.

analysisVersion.description: Version of everything that decides the result (ruleset, algorithms, catalog, database). Opaque: compare for equality only. Two checks of one client with the same marketplace, the same listing text and the same analysisVersion have the same result.

cached.description: True when the stored result of an identical earlier check is returned instead of a new analysis. Only a COMPLETE result is ever returned from the cache.

catalogStatus.description: SERVED when the text was compared with the catalog. NOT_CONFIGURED when the deployment serves no catalog and the check ran only the client's watchlist and the rules that need no catalog (ADR-031): the result is then INCOMPLETE, `skippedRuleIds` names the rules that did not run, and its absence of catalog findings says nothing.

catalogVersion.description: Version of the trademark catalog the text was compared with. Opaque. `none` when no catalog was served (`catalogStatus` NOT_CONFIGURED); a real catalog version is never `none`.

checkId.description: Identifier of the stored check; use it with GET /api/v1/trademark-checks/{id} until expiresAt.

completeness.description: COMPLETE when every rule ran. INCOMPLETE when a rule failed: the findings of the rules that succeeded are kept, failedRuleIds names the others, and riskLevel is the highest established level or UNKNOWN.

createdAt.description: When the check was first stored (UTC).

disclaimer.description: Statement that the result is a reference warning and not a legal conclusion. Show it with the result.

expiresAt.description: When the stored result stops being readable (UTC). After this instant GET answers 404 and the same listing is analysed again.

failedRuleIds.description: Rules that failed; empty for a COMPLETE result.

productType.description: The `product_type` the request named, as the ruleset declares it; null when the request named none (and for a result stored before product types existed).

riskLevel.description: The highest level among the findings (LOW when a complete check found nothing above LOW). UNKNOWN means the risk could not be determined because the check is INCOMPLETE; it is never reported as LOW.

rulesetVersion.description: Version of the trademark ruleset that produced the result.

skippedRuleIds.description: Rules that did not run because no catalog is served (`catalogStatus` NOT_CONFIGURED); empty otherwise.

watchlist.description: The client's watchlist the check used (ADR-031); null when the client had no enabled entry.

end.description: End of the span (UTF-16 code units, exclusive).

field.description: Which value the finding is about.

insideColorPhrase.description: The match lies inside a color phrase; this explains the finding and never lowers its risk.

label.description: The label the client gave the value, or null.

mark.description: The catalog mark that matched (catalog data); null for a finding without a mark.

message.description: Human text, currently Vietnamese. Names the mark and the position, not the buyer's text.

otherRuleIds.description: Other rules that matched an overlapping span and lost to this one.

risk.description: Risk of this finding: LOW, MEDIUM or HIGH.

score.description: Similarity from 0 to 1 for a fuzzy match, 1 for an exact or phrase match; null otherwise.

sourceIds.description: Ids of the source records of the matched catalog mark.

start.description: Start of the span in the text as sent (UTF-16 code units, inclusive).

suggestion.description: Human text, currently Vietnamese. Never proposes a replacement value.

completeness.description: Results per completeness; both values are present.

pack.description: The pack id; present on the period totals only.

riskLevels.description: Results per stored risk level; the four levels are always present.

topMarks.description: The catalog marks matched most often; present on the period totals only.

catalogVersion.description: The catalog version the scan used; null when it did not run.

failedRuleIds.description: Trademark rules that failed; empty when none did.

riskLevel.description: LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH or UNKNOWN. UNKNOWN means the risk could not be determined and is never LOW. No finding means only that the scanner found nothing in its catalog; it is no legal conclusion.

status.description: COMPLETE; INCOMPLETE (a trademark rule failed, findings kept); NOT_CONFIGURED (no catalog is served, so the scan did not run).

revision.description: Grows by one at every change; 0 when the client never had a list. It is the ETag, and `If-Match` on PUT compares it.

updatedAt.description: When the list last changed (UTC); null when it never existed.

version.description: SHA-256 of the enabled entries, the `watchlist.version` a trademark check reports; null when no entry is enabled (checks then use no watchlist).

addedBy.description: Who added it: `console:<account id>` or `api-key:<key id>`.

aliases.description: Other ways the mark is written: nicknames, short forms, slogans. Optional.

enabled.description: False keeps the entry in the list without scanning for it. Default true.

mark.description: The mark, as it should be reported. It identifies the entry: after normalization (case, accents, punctuation, look-alike letters) no two marks or aliases of one list may be equal.

niceClasses.description: Nice classes (1 to 45) the client notes for the mark. Shown in findings; they do not change a level.

note.description: Why the entry is listed, for example a claim received. Shown in the finding's message.

serialNumber.description: A USPTO serial number (eight digits), optional. A finding then carries the source id `uspto:<serialNumber>` and its look-up link.

maxTextChars.description: Longest mark or alias, in characters.

maxTokens.description: Most words in one mark or alias after normalization.

entryId.description: The entry's id, as `GET /api/v1/trademark-watchlist` shows it.

matchedAlias.description: The alias that matched; null when the mark itself did.

niceClasses.description: The Nice classes the client noted; they do not change the level.

note.description: Why the client listed the entry.

entries.description: Every entry of the list, in the order to keep. An empty list removes every entry.
How many enabled entries were looked for.

revision.description: The watchlist's revision when the check ran.

version.description: SHA-256 of the enabled entries; part of `analysisVersion`.

checkedAt.description: When this deployment asked the TSDR (or read a file saved from it) (UTC).

sourceId.description: The source id the status is for.

info.description:
Checks a marketplace listing before it is published and returns findings with suggestions. It only checks and suggests: it never edits a listing and never publishes anything.

Every endpoint except GET /health needs the X-API-Key header. Errors are RFC 7807 problem responses (application/problem+json) with a stable `code`; quote the `requestId` when reporting one. See docs/integration-guide.md for the calling flow, error table and field path conventions.

Every /api/v1 response carries X-Listing-Guard-Version, the release of the server. Inside /api/v1 changes are additive only (ADR-022): ignore unknown fields and accept unknown enum values. The contract of each release is attached to its GitHub Release (openapi.json, input-schema.json, contract-sha256.txt).

post.description: Takes the images of one listing as `multipart/form-data` and checks each against the image profile of the marketplace (see docs/input-schema.md, "Image checks"). Two kinds of part: `metadata`, a JSON object with the marketplace, an optional profile and one `{role, source}` entry per image, and one `images` file part per image, in the same order. Images are never fetched from a URL or read from a path. The format is read from the bytes (JPEG and PNG), never from the file name or the content type. An image that cannot be read (corrupt, unsupported, CMYK, too many pixels) is not an error of the request: it is answered as an INCOMPLETE image and the others are still checked. A threshold the marketplace ruleset does not have yet also makes a check INCOMPLETE and names it in `failedRules`; the shipped rulesets have none until the maintainer has reviewed the official pages, so every check of such a ruleset is INCOMPLETE and no verdict is given. `source` is only the caller's declaration; a CUSTOMER_CONTENT image gets a warning to check it by hand for third-party logos or marks (nothing here recognizes a logo, and no finding does not mean an image is free of one). The result is a reference warning, not a statement of the marketplace; show the `disclaimer` with it. If the same client already sent the same images and metadata with the same analysisVersion and the stored result is complete and still retained, it is returned with `cached: true`. An INCOMPLETE result is stored so its id can be read again, and is never reused for another request. A new complete result counts one unit of the client's monthly quota where plans are on (see `GET /api/v1/usage`); a cached or an INCOMPLETE one costs nothing. Results are kept for a limited time (`expiresAt`); the images and their file names are never stored, only their hashes, what was read from them and the findings. Off by default: a deployment that has not enabled it answers 503 `image-checks-not-configured`.

post.description: Takes the text a buyer typed for a custom product (a name, a number), one entry per field of the order, and a print profile (see docs/input-schema.md, "Personalization screening"). It is meant for the step before an order goes into production, not for listings. Two independent answers: the character rules (characters the print profile cannot print, a text that is too long, stray spaces) in `findings`, and the trademark scan of the same text in `trademark`. Show both; neither replaces the other. If no trademark catalog is served, the character rules still run and `trademark.status` is NOT_CONFIGURED with `riskLevel` UNKNOWN (UNKNOWN is never LOW), and the result is INCOMPLETE. The result is a reference warning built on an internal print policy and a catalog, not a statement of the print workshop, a marketplace or a court; show the `disclaimer` with it. It proposes no replacement and changes no text. The answer never repeats the text; use the offsets (UTF-16 code units) to find a finding in it. If the same client already sent the same values with the same analysisVersion and the stored result is complete and still retained, it is returned with `cached: true`. An INCOMPLETE result is stored so its id can be read again, and is never reused for another request. A new complete result counts one unit of the client's monthly quota where plans are on (see `GET /api/v1/usage`); a cached or an INCOMPLETE one costs nothing. Results are kept for a limited time (`expiresAt`); the text the buyer typed is never stored, only its hash and the result.

get.description:
Adds up what the client has stored: results per pack, the rules with the most findings, the trademark risk levels and the catalog marks matched most often, and the same numbers per ISO week. It counts; it never returns or reads text a client typed (a listing, a tag, a buyer's text): only counts, enumerations, rule ids, catalog marks and version strings.

`from` and `to` are UTC dates, both included, and both are required. The longest period is set by the deployment (92 days by default). A period with no data is a `200` with zeros.

A "check" is a stored result: a cached answer creates no row, so a listing checked again with the same analysis is counted once, and there is no cache-hit number. The packs `trademark-risk`, `variation-checks` and `personalization-screening` delete their results after a retention period and count only what is still stored; `coverageNote` says from which day their numbers are complete. `listing-rules` results are not deleted.

It is read only, needs no plan pack, costs no unit of the quota and is never cached (`Cache-Control: no-store`).

post.description: Takes the request of `POST /api/v1/checks` (`marketplace` and `listing` in the marketplace's own format) and an optional `product_type`, so a client can send one JSON to both endpoints (`/checks` ignores `product_type`). Compares the listing's text with the configured trademark catalog and returns findings with evidence: the field, the span in the text the API worked on (after trimming and Unicode NFC, UTF-16 offsets), the matched mark and how it matched. With a `product_type`, a mark whose Nice classes are not the product type's is reported one level lower, and `riskAdjustments` says why and from which level; a mark that is an ordinary word of the ruleset's list is capped the same way unless it is the brand. `sourceLinks` gives a public look-up page for the source records the ruleset has an address for. The result is a reference warning, not a legal conclusion; show the `disclaimer` with it. If the same client already sent the same listing text and product type with the same analysisVersion and the stored result is complete and still retained, it is returned with `cached: true`. An INCOMPLETE result (a rule failed) is stored so its id can be read again, and is never reused for another request. A new complete result counts one unit of the client's monthly quota where plans are on (see `GET /api/v1/usage`); a cached or an INCOMPLETE one costs nothing. Results are kept for a limited time (`expiresAt`); only the listing's hash and the result are stored, not the listing text.
